source_text:
ὑπὲρ πάντα θεὸν ἢ σέβασμα ὑπεραιρόμενον, οἷον ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν
εἰδωλολατρείαν· ὥσπερ γὰρ αὐτὸς αὐτὴν συνεστήσατο, οὕτω καὶ αὐτὸς ἀνατρέψει
αὐτὴν ἐλθών, καὶ πᾶσαν αἵρεσιν, ἣν ἀντέθηκε τῷ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας, ἵνα καὶ κατὰ
τοῦτο κατακριθῶσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ὅτι τὰ εἴδωλα ἐφ' οἷς ἐπλανήθησαν, οὐκ αὐτοὶ
καθεῖλον, ἀλλ' ὁ πλανήσας. τὰς δὲ πλάνας ταύτας ἐξ ἀρχῆς συνεστήσατο ὁ διάβολος,
ἀφιστῶν τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ βραχὺ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους καὶ ἠρέμα τὴν ἑαυτοῦ προσκύνησιν
ἀντεισάγων, ἵνα ὅταν μετὰ ταῦτα ἔλθῃ, πεπλανημένους αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐκτὸς ὄντας τῆς
τοῦ θεοῦ βοηθείας, εὐχερῶς ὑπαγάγηται ἑαυτῷ. περὶ δὲ τῆς ἐσομένης πλάνης τῶν
ἀνθρώπων καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ σωτὴρ προεῖπεν ὅτι δυσχερὲς ἐλθόντα αὐτὸν εὑρεῖν τὴν
πίστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας, τοῦτ' ἔστι ὁ ἀντίχριστος· ἥξει γὰρ εἰς
Ἱεροσόλυμα ὡς ἀνοικοδομήσων τὸν ναόν, καὶ στήσεται ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ τόπῳ θεὸν
ἑαυτὸν ἀναγορεύων. ὁ ἀντικείμενος καὶ ὑπεραιρόμενος ὑπὲρ πάντα μὲν λεγόμενον
θεόν, ἀντὶ τοῦ ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν εἰδωλολατρείαν· ὑπὲρ δὲ πᾶν σέβασμα, ἀντὶ τοῦ πᾶσαν
334 αἵρεσιν ἣν ἀντέθηκε τῷ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας. ὥσπερ ὑποσκευὴ ἁψῖδος, οὕτως αἱ
αἱρέσεις παρὰ τοῖς λεγομένοις καὶ Ἰουδαίοις καὶ Ἕλλησι προπαρασκευή εἰσι τῷ
διαβόλῳ. καὶ ὥσπερ ἁψῖδος σφιγχθείσης καὶ λαβούσης τὴν οἰκείαν κατασκευὴν ἡ
ὑποσκευὴ λύεται, καὶ μένει μόνη ἡ ἁψὶς στερεά, οὕτως ὁ διάβολος τὰς αἱρέσεις τὰς
πολλὰς καὶ τὰς τῆς πλάνης ὁδοὺς ἀντὶ ὑποσκευῆς ὑπέθηκεν ὥσπερ ἁψῖδά τινα τὴν
ἑαυτοῦ προσκύνησιν ἐπισκευάσας. 333, col 2 ∆ιὰ τούτου δείκνυσιν ὅτι τὴν
εἰδωλολατρίαν ἣν ὁ διάβολος συνεστήσατο, αὐτὸς ἐλθὼν ἀνατρέπει. καὶ πᾶσαν
αἵρεσιν ἣν ἀντέθηκεν τῷ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας, αὐτὸς ἐλθὼν παραλύει, ἵνα καὶ ἐν
τούτῳ τὸ κρίμα ἔχωσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ὅτι τὰ ἐφ' οἷς ἐπλανήθησαν οὐκ αὐτοὶ
καθεῖλον, ἀλλ' ὁ πλανῶν αὐτούς.
thought_title: The devil's scaffolding: idolatry and heresies prepare his own worship
orientation: Severian is explaining Paul's phrase about the man of lawlessness exalting himself above every so-called god or object of worship, showing how the devil will overthrow the very idolatry and heresies he himself set up.
pass_a_gloss: being exalted above every god or object of worship, that is, above all idolatry; for just as he himself established it, so also he himself will overturn it when he comes, and every heresy, which he set against the word of truth, so that in this too humans may be condemned, because the idols on which they were deceived, they themselves did not pull down, but the deceiver did. These errors from the beginning the devil established, drawing humans away from God little by little and gently introducing his own worship, so that when after these things he comes, having found them deceived and being outside the help of God, he may easily bring them under himself. About the future error of humans the Savior himself also foretold that it is difficult for him, when he comes, to find faith on the earth. The man of lawlessness, that is the antichrist; for he will come to Jerusalem as one about to rebuild the temple, and he will stand in the holy place proclaiming himself god. The one who opposes and is exalted above every so-called god, instead of above all idolatry; and above every object of worship, instead of every heresy which he set against the word of truth. Just as scaffolding for an arch, so the heresies among those called both Jews and Greeks are a preparation for the devil. And just as when the arch is compressed and receives its proper construction, the scaffolding is loosened, and the arch alone remains solid, so the devil placed the many heresies and the paths of error as scaffolding, having prepared his own worship as a kind of arch. Through this he shows that the idolatry which the devil established, he himself when he comes overturns. And every heresy which he set against the word of truth, he himself when he comes dissolves, so that in this too humans may have judgment, because the things on which they were deceived they themselves did not pull down, but the one deceiving them did.

pass_b_english: He exalts himself above every god or object of worship—that is, above every form of idolatry. For just as the devil himself established idolatry, so he himself will overturn it when he comes, along with every heresy he has set against the word of truth. And in this too people will be condemned: the idols over which they were deceived were not torn down by them, but by the deceiver himself. The devil established these deceptions from the beginning, drawing people away from God little by little and quietly introducing his own worship in its place, so that when he comes afterward he may easily bring them under himself, since they are already deceived and cut off from God's help. The Savior himself also foretold the deception that would come upon people, saying that when he comes he will scarcely find faith on the earth. The man of lawlessness—that is, the antichrist—will come to Jerusalem as though to rebuild the temple, and he will stand in the holy place proclaiming himself God. He is the one who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god, meaning above every form of idolatry, and above every object of worship, meaning every heresy he has set against the word of truth. As scaffolding for an arch, so the heresies among those called both Jews and Greeks are a preparation for the devil. And just as when an arch is compressed and receives its proper construction the scaffolding is removed and the arch alone remains solid, so the devil has laid down the many heresies and the paths of error as scaffolding, having constructed his own worship like an arch. Through this it is shown that the idolatry the devil established, he himself will overturn when he comes. And every heresy he set against the word of truth, he himself will dissolve when he comes, so that in this too people will have their judgment: the things over which they were deceived were not torn down by them, but by the one who deceives them.

problems.quote: Through this Paul shows that the idolatry the devil established, he himself will overturn when he comes.
problems.source_quote: Διὰ τοῦτο δείκνυσιν ὅτι τὴν εἰδωλολατρίαν ἣν ὁ διάβολος συνέστησεν, αὐτὸς ἐλθὼν ἀνατρέπει.
problems.why: Source does not mention Paul; the showing is presented without attributing it to Paul.
problems.fix: Through this it is shown that the idolatry the devil established, he himself will overturn when he comes.

fixed: Removed 'Paul' from the final paragraph: the source's 'Διὰ τοῦτο δείκνυσιν' has no named subject, so 'it is shown' is correct.

problems.quote: the idols by which they were deceived were not torn down by them, but by the deceiver himself
problems.source_quote: ὅτι τὰ εἴδωλα ἐφ' οἷς ἐπλανήθησαν, οὐκ αὐτοὶ καθεῖλον, ἀλλ' ὁ πλανήσας
problems.why: Source says 'the idols on which they were deceived'; English 'by which they were deceived' changes the relationship—source suggests they were deceived concerning/over the idols, not 'by' the idols as agents.
problems.fix: the idols over which they were deceived they did not tear down themselves, but the deceiver
problems.ruling: Greek 'ἐφ' οἷς' = 'concerning which', not 'by which' (idols aren't agents)

problems.quote: the things by which they were deceived were not torn down by them, but by the one who deceives them
problems.source_quote: ὅτι τὰ ἐφ' οἷς ἐπλανήθησαν οὐκ αὐτοὶ καθεῖλον, ἀλλ' ὁ πλανῶν αὐτούς
problems.why: Same issue: 'ἐφ' οἷς' means 'over which' or 'concerning which,' not 'by which.' Also 'the one who deceives them' is present participle, but 'deceiver' earlier was aorist participle ὁ πλανήσας; here it's ὁ πλανῶν. English obscures this distinction but meaning similar.
problems.fix: the things over which they were deceived they did not tear down themselves, but the one who deceives them
problems.ruling: Same preposition issue; 'ἐφ' οἷς' not 'by which' changes agency

problems.why: The source contains no scripture citation. The English adds '(Luke 18:8)' without source support. This is a wrong_scripture/addition error since the source quotes no verse reference.
problems.ruling: Source contains no biblical citation; adding (Luke 18:8) is unwarranted

problems.quote: preparing his own worship as though it were an arch
problems.source_quote: ὥσπερ ἁψῖδά τινα τὴν ἑαυτοῦ προσκύνησιν ἐπισκευάσας
problems.why: 'ἐπισκευάσας' means 'constructing, building, repairing'—the devil is building his worship using heresies as scaffolding. 'Preparing' is weak; more importantly, the syntax 'preparing his own worship as though it were an arch' inverts the image: he constructs his worship like an arch, using heresies as scaffolding for it.
problems.fix: having constructed his own worship like an arch
problems.ruling: Greek shows worship built like an arch; English 'preparing ... as though it were an arch' reverses metaphor

problems.quote: the things by which they were deceived
problems.why: Same 'ἐφ' οἷς' issue: 'over which' not 'by which.'
problems.fix: the things over which they were deceived
problems.ruling: Again 'ἐφ' οἷς' means 'over which', not 'by which'

problems.quote: He is exalted above every god or object of worship
problems.source_quote: ὑπὲρ πάντα θεὸν ἢ σέβασμα ὑπεραιρόμενον
problems.why: ὑπεραιρόμενον is middle ('exalting himself'), not passive ('is exalted'); the English loses the antichrist's self-exaltation.
problems.fix: He exalts himself above every god or object of worship
problems.ruling: ὑπεραιρόμενον is middle (self-raising); passive “is exalted” drops reflexive agency over θεὸν/σέβασμα.

problems.quote: He is the one who opposes and is exalted
problems.why: ὑπεραιρόμενος is middle ('exalts himself'), not passive ('is exalted'); the English turns his self-exaltation into a passive state.
problems.fix: He is the one who opposes and exalts himself
problems.ruling: ὑπεραιρόμενος is middle in ὁ ἀντικείμενος καὶ…; “is exalted” misstates self-exaltation as passive state.

last_rejected.quote: saying that when he comes he will scarcely find faith on the earth
last_rejected.source_quote: περὶ δὲ τῆς ἐσομένης πλάνης τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ σωτὴρ προεῖπεν ὅτι δυσχερὲς ἐλθόντα αὐτὸν εὑρεῖν τὴν πίστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
last_rejected.why: The Greek says 'when he comes' referring to the Savior/Christ, but the English 'when he comes' is ambiguous and could mislead readers into thinking the antichrist is the subject.
last_rejected.fix: saying that when the Son of Man comes he will scarcely find faith on the earth
last_rejected.ruling: Greek ἐλθόντα αὐτὸν ties 'when he comes' to the Savior; English ambiguity does not change meaning given context.

last_rejected.quote: among those called both Jews and Greeks
last_rejected.source_quote: παρὰ τοῖς λεγομένοις καὶ Ἰουδαίοις καὶ Ἕλλησι
last_rejected.why: Source names three groups; English merges τοῖς λεγομένοις with Jews and Greeks.
last_rejected.fix: among those so called, and among Jews, and among Greeks
last_rejected.ruling: τοῖς λεγομένοις governs καὶ Ἰουδαίοις καὶ Ἕλλησι ('both Jews and Greeks'); the Greek names two groups, not three, so nothing is omitted.
